Guidance & outlook: The organised segment is expected to grow faster than the unorganised segment, with projected CAGRs of roughly 15% and 9% respectively over FY 2025-30.
The domestic textile and apparel market has expanded from USD 106 billion in FY 2019-20 to USD 157 billion in FY 2025-26, a CAGR of around 7%.
The Ministry of Textiles has set an ambitious target of USD 250 billion by FY 2030-31, which will require growth to accelerate to approximately 9% per annum.
Growth & demand: India's economy continued to outperform most major economies in FY 2025-26, delivering real GDP growth of 7.7% (second advance estimates, National Statistical Office), underpinned by robust domestic demand, sustained government capital expenditure and steady private investment.

Looking ahead the IMF and the RBI project India's GDP growth at about 6.5 - 6.8% for the FY 2026-27, keeping India the fastest growing major economy and well above the roughly 3% projected global growth rate.
Real GDP growth in FY 2025-26 is estimated to be 7.7% with a March quarter growth of around 7.8%.
Margins & costs: The IMF raised its 2026 global inflation forecast to 4.4%, driven by surging oil, gas, and fertilizer costs.

The key near-term risk continues to be the West Asia conflict: higher energy prices, increased freight costs and supply-chain disruptions could raise input costs and weigh on inflation and consumer sentiment.
